policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the verb as 'shall not fear'; this distinguishes the qere יִרְאֶה from the ketiv reading reflected by the note's 'see'.
ASV has the plural 'according to his ways', distinguishing qere כִּדְרָכָיו from singular ketiv כדרכו.
ASV renders the plural 'in the midst of his days', distinguishing qere יָמָיו from ketiv ימו.
ASV's 'They that depart from me' directly renders qere וְסוּרַי and does not permit ketiv יסורי.
ASV renders the definite phrase 'the children of the people', distinguishing qere הָעָם from ketiv עם; the alternative-rendering note does not decide a reading.
ASV renders the infinitival construction 'that they might not hear', distinguishing qere שְׁמוֹעַ from ketiv שומע.
ASV's 'to hallow the sabbath day, to do no work therein' makes 'therein' refer to the masculine sabbath day, distinguishing qere בּוֹ from feminine ketiv בה.
